Queries

activeChannel

Description

The active Channel

Response

Returns a Channel!

Example

Query
query activeChannel {
  activeChannel {
    id
    createdAt
    updatedAt
    code
    token
    defaultTaxZone {
      ...ZoneFragment
    }
    defaultShippingZone {
      ...ZoneFragment
    }
    defaultLanguageCode
    availableLanguageCodes
    currencyCode
    defaultCurrencyCode
    availableCurrencyCodes
    trackInventory
    outOfStockThreshold
    pricesIncludeTax
    seller {
      ...SellerFragment
    }
    customFields {
      ...ChannelCustomFieldsFragment
    }
  }
}
Response
{
  "data": {
    "activeChannel": {
      "id": 4,
      "createdAt": "2007-12-03T10:15:30Z",
      "updatedAt": "2007-12-03T10:15:30Z",
      "code": "abc123",
      "token": "xyz789",
      "defaultTaxZone": Zone,
      "defaultShippingZone": Zone,
      "defaultLanguageCode": "af",
      "availableLanguageCodes": ["af"],
      "currencyCode": "AED",
      "defaultCurrencyCode": "AED",
      "availableCurrencyCodes": ["AED"],
      "trackInventory": true,
      "outOfStockThreshold": 123,
      "pricesIncludeTax": true,
      "seller": Seller,
      "customFields": ChannelCustomFields
    }
  }
}

Queries

activeOrder

Description

The active Order. Will be null until an Order is created via addItemToOrder. Once an Order reaches the state of PaymentAuthorized or PaymentSettled, then that Order is no longer considered "active" and this query will once again return null.

Response

Returns an Order

Example

Query
query activeOrder {
  activeOrder {
    id
    createdAt
    updatedAt
    type
    orderPlacedAt
    code
    state
    active
    customer {
      ...CustomerFragment
    }
    shippingAddress {
      ...OrderAddressFragment
    }
    billingAddress {
      ...OrderAddressFragment
    }
    lines {
      ...OrderLineFragment
    }
    surcharges {
      ...SurchargeFragment
    }
    discounts {
      ...DiscountFragment
    }
    couponCodes
    promotions {
      ...PromotionFragment
    }
    payments {
      ...PaymentFragment
    }
    fulfillments {
      ...FulfillmentFragment
    }
    totalQuantity
    subTotal
    subTotalWithTax
    currencyCode
    shippingLines {
      ...ShippingLineFragment
    }
    shipping
    shippingWithTax
    total
    totalWithTax
    taxSummary {
      ...OrderTaxSummaryFragment
    }
    history {
      ...HistoryEntryListFragment
    }
    deliveryGroups {
      ...DeliveryCredentialGroupFragment
    }
    customFields {
      ...OrderCustomFieldsFragment
    }
  }
}
Response
{
  "data": {
    "activeOrder": {
      "id": 4,
      "createdAt": "2007-12-03T10:15:30Z",
      "updatedAt": "2007-12-03T10:15:30Z",
      "type": "Regular",
      "orderPlacedAt": "2007-12-03T10:15:30Z",
      "code": "abc123",
      "state": "abc123",
      "active": false,
      "customer": Customer,
      "shippingAddress": OrderAddress,
      "billingAddress": OrderAddress,
      "lines": [OrderLine],
      "surcharges": [Surcharge],
      "discounts": [Discount],
      "couponCodes": ["abc123"],
      "promotions": [Promotion],
      "payments": [Payment],
      "fulfillments": [Fulfillment],
      "totalQuantity": 123,
      "subTotal": Money,
      "subTotalWithTax": Money,
      "currencyCode": "AED",
      "shippingLines": [ShippingLine],
      "shipping": Money,
      "shippingWithTax": Money,
      "total": Money,
      "totalWithTax": Money,
      "taxSummary": [OrderTaxSummary],
      "history": HistoryEntryList,
      "deliveryGroups": [DeliveryCredentialGroup],
      "customFields": OrderCustomFields
    }
  }
}

addItemToOrder

Description

Adds an item to the Order. If custom fields are defined on the OrderLine entity, a third argument 'customFields' will be available.

Response

Returns an UpdateOrderItemsResult!

Arguments
Name Description
productVariantId - ID!
quantity - Int!

Example

Query
mutation addItemToOrder(
  $productVariantId: ID!,
  $quantity: Int!
) {
  addItemToOrder(
    productVariantId: $productVariantId,
    quantity: $quantity
  ) {
    ... on Order {
      ...OrderFragment
    }
    ... on OrderModificationError {
      ...OrderModificationErrorFragment
    }
    ... on OrderLimitError {
      ...OrderLimitErrorFragment
    }
    ... on NegativeQuantityError {
      ...NegativeQuantityErrorFragment
    }
    ... on InsufficientStockError {
      ...InsufficientStockErrorFragment
    }
    ... on OrderInterceptorError {
      ...OrderInterceptorErrorFragment
    }
  }
}

{"productVariantId": "4", "quantity": 123}
Response
{"data": {"addItemToOrder": Order}}

      }

login

Description

Authenticates the user using the native authentication strategy. This mutation is an alias for authenticate({ native: { ... }})

The rememberMe option applies when using cookie-based sessions, and if true it will set the maxAge of the session cookie to 1 year.

Response

Returns a NativeAuthenticationResult!

Arguments
Name Description
username - String!
password - String!
rememberMe - Boolean

Example

Query
mutation login(
  $username: String!,
  $password: String!,
  $rememberMe: Boolean
) {
  login(
    username: $username,
    password: $password,
    rememberMe: $rememberMe
  ) {
    ... on CurrentUser {
      ...CurrentUserFragment
    }
    ... on InvalidCredentialsError {
      ...InvalidCredentialsErrorFragment
    }
    ... on NotVerifiedError {
      ...NotVerifiedErrorFragment
    }
    ... on NativeAuthStrategyError {
      ...NativeAuthStrategyErrorFragment
    }
  }
}

}

Mutations

registerCustomerAccount

Description

Register a Customer account with the given credentials. There are three possible registration flows:

If authOptions.requireVerification is set to true:

  1. The Customer is registered with a password. A verificationToken will be created (and typically emailed to the Customer). That verificationToken would then be passed to the verifyCustomerAccount mutation without a password. The Customer is then verified and authenticated in one step.
  2. The Customer is registered without a password. A verificationToken will be created (and typically emailed to the Customer). That verificationToken would then be passed to the verifyCustomerAccount mutation with the chosen password of the Customer. The Customer is then verified and authenticated in one step.

If authOptions.requireVerification is set to false:

  1. The Customer must be registered with a password. No further action is needed - the Customer is able to authenticate immediately.
Response

Returns a RegisterCustomerAccountResult!

Arguments
Name Description
input - RegisterCustomerInput!

Example

Query
mutation registerCustomerAccount($input: RegisterCustomerInput!) {
  registerCustomerAccount(input: $input) {
    ... on Success {
      ...SuccessFragment
    }
    ... on MissingPasswordError {
      ...MissingPasswordErrorFragment
    }
    ... on PasswordValidationError {
      ...PasswordValidationErrorFragment
    }
    ... on NativeAuthStrategyError {
      ...NativeAuthStrategyErrorFragment
    }
  }
}
Variables
{"input": RegisterCustomerInput}
Response
{"data": {"registerCustomerAccount": Success}}

  ) {

Mutations

verifyCustomerAccount

Description

Verify a Customer email address with the token sent to that address. Only applicable if authOptions.requireVerification is set to true.

If the Customer was not registered with a password in the registerCustomerAccount mutation, the password must be provided here.

Response

Returns a VerifyCustomerAccountResult!

Arguments
Name Description
token - String!
password - String

Example

Query
mutation verifyCustomerAccount(
  $token: String!,
  $password: String
) {
  verifyCustomerAccount(
    token: $token,
    password: $password
  ) {
    ... on CurrentUser {
      ...CurrentUserFragment
    }
    ... on VerificationTokenInvalidError {
      ...VerificationTokenInvalidErrorFragment
    }
    ... on VerificationTokenExpiredError {
      ...VerificationTokenExpiredErrorFragment
    }
    ... on MissingPasswordError {
      ...MissingPasswordErrorFragment
    }
    ... on PasswordValidationError {
      ...PasswordValidationErrorFragment
    }
    ... on PasswordAlreadySetError {
      ...PasswordAlreadySetErrorFragment
    }
    ... on NativeAuthStrategyError {
      ...NativeAuthStrategyErrorFragment
    }
  }
}
Variables
{
  "token": "abc123",
  "password": "abc123"
}
Response
{"data": {"verifyCustomerAccount": CurrentUser}}

Types

FacetValueFilterInput

Description

Used to construct boolean expressions for filtering search results by FacetValue ID. Examples:

  • ID=1 OR ID=2: { facetValueFilters: [{ or: [1,2] }] }
  • ID=1 AND ID=2: { facetValueFilters: [{ and: 1 }, { and: 2 }] }
  • ID=1 AND (ID=2 OR ID=3): { facetValueFilters: [{ and: 1 }, { or: [2,3] }] }
Fields
Input Field Description
and - ID
or - [ID!]
Example
{"and": 4, "or": ["4"]}

Types

ID

Description

The ID scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as "4") or integer (such as 4) input value will be accepted as an ID.

Example
4

Description

in - [String!]

isNull - Boolean

  "notEq": "xyz789",
  "in": ["abc123"],
  "notIn": ["xyz789"],
  "isNull": false
}

The price of a single unit including discounts, excluding tax.

If Order-level discounts have been applied, this will not be the actual taxable unit price (see proratedUnitPrice), but is generally the correct price to display to customers to avoid confusion about the internal handling of distributed Order-level discounts.

Types

Permission

Description

@description Permissions for administrators and customers. Used to control access to GraphQL resolvers via the {@link Allow} decorator.

Understanding Permission.Owner

Permission.Owner is a special permission which is used in some Vendure resolvers to indicate that that resolver should only be accessible to the "owner" of that resource.

For example, the Shop API activeCustomer query resolver should only return the Customer object for the "owner" of that Customer, i.e. based on the activeUserId of the current session. As a result, the resolver code looks like this:

@example

\@Query()
\@Allow(Permission.Owner)
async activeCustomer(\@Ctx() ctx: RequestContext): Promise<Customer | undefined> {
  const userId = ctx.activeUserId;
  if (userId) {
    return this.customerService.findOneByUserId(ctx, userId);
  }
}

Here we can see that the "ownership" must be enforced by custom logic inside the resolver. Since "ownership" cannot be defined generally nor statically encoded at build-time, any resolvers using Permission.Owner must include logic to enforce that only the owner of the resource has access. If not, then it is the equivalent of using Permission.Public.

@docsCategory common

Values
Enum Value Description

Authenticated

 Authenticated means simply that the user is logged in

SuperAdmin

 SuperAdmin has unrestricted access to all operations

Owner

 Owner means the user owns this entity, e.g. a Customer's own Order

Public

 Public means any unauthenticated user may perform the operation

 Grants permission to update GlobalSettings

UpdateAddressInput

Description

Input used to update an Address.

The countryCode must correspond to a code property of a Country that has been defined in the Vendure server. The code property is typically a 2-character ISO code such as "GB", "US", "DE" etc. If an invalid code is passed, the mutation will fail.

Fields

company - String
streetLine1 - String
streetLine2 - String
city - String
province - String

countryCode - String

defaultShippingAddress - Boolean
defaultBillingAddress - Boolean
customFields - UpdateAddressCustomFieldsInput
